title: Transport of generator coefficient equations through finite expression contexts
statement:
Let $I$ be a set of indices. For each $s\in I$ let $\mathcal C_s,\mathcal D_s$ be categories [def-nagata-category] and let $R_s:\mathcal C_s\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_s:L_s$ be an adjoint equivalence with its specified unit $u$ and counit $e$. Choose a typed collection of unary functors $A:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal D_t$ and binary functors $B:\mathcal D_s\times\mathcal D_t\to\mathcal D_v$, together with corresponding functors $\bar A,\bar B$ on the $\mathcal C$ categories and natural isomorphisms $d_A:L_tAR_s\cong\bar A$, $d_B:L_vB(R_s-,R_t-)\cong\bar B$. These data may be restricted to full subcategories closed under all expressions under consideration.

For an input family $K_i\in\mathcal C_{s_i}$ and a finite typed expression $V$, put $M_V=V(RK_i)$ and let $\bar V$ be its evaluation in $\bar A,\bar B$. Use
$$a_A(M)=d_A(LM)(LA(e_M))^{-1},\qquad
 a_B(M,N)=d_B(LM,LN)(LB(e_M,e_N))^{-1}.$$
Suppose natural isomorphisms $c_V:LM_V\to\bar V(K_i)$ are given by $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$, $c_{AV}=\bar A(c_V)a_A(M_V)$ and $c_{B(V,T)}=\bar B(c_V,c_T)a_B(M_V,M_T)$. Let $r_V:R\bar V(K_i)\to M_V$ satisfy $r_V=e_{M_V}R(c_V^{-1})$.

For a natural transformation of expressions $\tau:V\to T$ and an independently specified natural transformation $\bar\tau:\bar V\to\bar T$, the whole-category coefficient equation
$$\tau_{RK_i}r_V=r_TR(\bar\tau_{K_i})$$
implies
$$c_TL(\tau_{RK_i})=\bar\tau_{K_i}c_V.$$
This latter equation persists under every finite unary and binary outer expression context, including changing either binary slot, changing both slots, repeated inputs, and composites and identities of transformations. Invertible transformations may also be inverted. Explicitly the context equation for $H$ is
$$c_{H[T]}L(H[\tau]_{RK_i})=\bar H[\bar\tau]_{K_i}c_{H[V]}.$$
Consequently every equality between composites of these generators and their contexts is taken by $L$ and conjugation with the prescribed $c$ to the corresponding equality between the independently specified barred transformations. The comparisons used for both routes are the recursive ones with the same parentheses. No faithfulness assumption on evaluation functors, no lifting of component arrows, and no invertibility of $\tau$ are required.

proof.text: Write composition right to left and suppress sort subscripts only when uniquely typed. In the specified adjoint equivalence $R:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $L:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, the natural isomorphisms have types $u_X:X\to LRX$ and $e_M:RLM\to M$. Functors preserve identities and composition; a natural transformation $b:F\to G$ means $G(h)b_X=b_YF(h)$. An inverse isomorphism satisfies both inverse equations. We use precisely these defining equations, and associativity and identity laws from [def-nagata-category]. In particular a functor carries an inverse to an inverse, since applying it to the two inverse equations gives the two required identities.

proof.text:
Put $h=\tau_{RK_i}:M_V\to M_T$ and $k=\bar\tau_{K_i}:\bar V(K_i)\to\bar T(K_i)$. Substitute the assumed formulas for $r_V,r_T$ into the coefficient equation. Naturality of $e$ at $h$ gives $h e_{M_V}=e_{M_T}RL(h)$, so that equation becomes
$$e_{M_T}R(L(h)c_V^{-1})=e_{M_T}R(c_T^{-1}k).$$
Compose on the left with $e_{M_T}^{-1}$ to obtain $R(L(h)c_V^{-1})=R(c_T^{-1}k)$. Both arguments of $R$ are arrows $\bar V(K_i)\to LM_T$ in the same category $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: For arrows $f,g:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal C$, naturality of the invertible unit gives $f=u_Y^{-1}LR(f)u_X$ and $g=u_Y^{-1}LR(g)u_X$. Thus $R(f)=R(g)$ implies $f=g$ by applying $L$ and these formulas. Apply this calculation to the two arrows from step 2. It gives $L(h)c_V^{-1}=c_T^{-1}k$; multiplying by $c_T$ on the left and $c_V$ on the right yields $c_TL(h)=kc_V$. This derives the generator equation without assuming that $h$ is invertible or that any evaluation functor detects equality.

proof.text:
For a unary symbol $A:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal D_t$, put $E_A(M)=L_tA(e_{s,M})$. If $h:M\to N$, naturality of $e_s$, followed by $L_tA$, gives
$$L_tA(h)E_A(M)=E_A(N)L_tAR_sL_s(h).$$
Naturality of $d_A$ gives $d_A(L_sN)L_tAR_sL_s(h)=\bar A(L_s(h))d_A(L_sM)$. Multiply the first equality by inverses of $E_A(N)$ and $E_A(M)$ and insert the second. The result is
$$a_A(N)L_tA(h)=\bar A(L_s(h))a_A(M).$$
All inverses exist because $e_s$ and $d_A$ are natural isomorphisms; this is exactly naturality of the $a_A$ prescribed in the statement.

proof.text:
For a binary symbol $B:\mathcal D_s\times\mathcal D_t\to\mathcal D_v$, write $P=(M,N)$, $P'=(M',N')$, $q=(h,j):P\to P'$ and $E_B(P)=L_vB(e_{s,M},e_{t,N})$. The pair of counit naturality equations, after applying the functor $L_vB$ on the product category, reads
$$L_vB(h,j)E_B(P)=E_B(P')L_vB(R_sL_s(h),R_tL_t(j)).$$
Naturality of $d_B$ reads
$$d_B(L_sM',L_tN')L_vB(R_sL_s(h),R_tL_t(j))=\bar B(L_s(h),L_t(j))d_B(L_sM,L_tN).$$
As in step 4, multiplying by the two $E_B$ inverses gives
$$a_B(P')L_vB(h,j)=\bar B(L_s(h),L_t(j))a_B(P).$$
This is a single naturality calculation on the product category, so it allows arbitrary arrows in both slots.

proof.text:
We now induct on the finite outer expression context, permitting several occurrences of its hole. The inductive assertion for a pair of evaluated expressions $V,T$ and arrows $h:M_V\to M_T$, $k:\bar V\to\bar T$ is $c_TL(h)=kc_V$. At a hole it is step 3. At an unchanged input or unchanged subexpression take $h=1$ and $k=1$; the assertion is $c_V=c_V$ by functoriality. At a unary constructor, assuming the assertion for its child, step 4 and the prescribed recursion give
$$c_{AT}L(A(h))=\bar A(c_T)a_A(M_T)L(A(h))=\bar A(c_TL(h))a_A(M_V)=\bar A(k)\bar A(c_V)a_A(M_V)=\bar A(k)c_{AV}.$$
The middle equality uses the child's assertion and the functor composition law.

proof.text:
At a binary constructor take child arrows $h:M_V\to M_T$, $j:M_W\to M_U$ and barred arrows $k:\bar V\to\bar T$, $l:\bar W\to\bar U$, with $c_TL_s(h)=kc_V$ and $c_UL_t(j)=lc_W$. Step 5 and the recursion give
$$\begin{aligned}c_{B(T,U)}L_vB(h,j)&=\bar B(c_T,c_U)a_B(M_T,M_U)L_vB(h,j)\\&=\bar B(c_TL_s(h),c_UL_t(j))a_B(M_V,M_W)\\&=\bar B(k,l)\bar B(c_V,c_W)a_B(M_V,M_W)\\&=\bar B(k,l)c_{B(V,W)}.\end{aligned}$$
One unchanged slot is the identity case of step 6; two changed slots use both child assertions. Distinct occurrences of a repeated input or repeated hole use the same arrow in each occurrence. The pair $(h,h)$ is a valid morphism in a product category, so no disjointness condition is used. These are all constructors of a finite typed context, completing the induction and proving the displayed context equation.

proof.text:
The relation also closes under composition: if $c_TL(h)=kc_V$ and $c_UL(j)=lc_T$, then
$$c_UL(jh)=c_UL(j)L(h)=lc_TL(h)=lkc_V.$$
Identities satisfy $c_VL(1)=1c_V$. Applying the same calculation to any finite composable list proves the relation for all composites, with the specified endpoint comparisons.

proof.text: If $h$ is invertible, the established relation says $k=c_TL(h)c_V^{-1}$. Its inverse is therefore $c_VL(h^{-1})c_T^{-1}$: multiplying either way and using the functor image of $hh^{-1}=1=h^{-1}h$ gives the identity. Consequently $c_VL(h^{-1})=k^{-1}c_T$, the relation for the inverse transformation. Applied componentwise to an invertible natural transformation, this uses its natural inverse; that inverse is natural by multiplying the original naturality square by the component inverses.

proof.text:
For a generator, context, identity, composite or allowed inverse $p:V\to W$ with independently specified barred expression-map $\bar p$, steps 3 and 6–9 give
$$\bar p_{K_i}=c_WL(p_{RK_i})c_V^{-1}.$$
If two such composites $p,q:V\to W$ are equal as transformations, evaluate the equality at $RK_i$, apply $L$, and multiply by these same endpoint comparisons. The displayed formula gives $\bar p_{K_i}=\bar q_{K_i}$ for every input family, which is equality of the barred natural transformations by their definition as component families. The induction always used the recursive $c$ for the exact parenthesized syntax tree, so both routes use those prescribed comparisons. No reassociation identification is inserted.

proof.text: Every calculation is componentwise in the chosen categories and uses only the stipulated functors, their natural transformations, and inverses of the comparison components. In a restriction to full subcategories on which these data and the expressions are defined, the same arrows and equations remain in the same Hom sets, so the calculations apply verbatim. Empty categories give vacuous component assertions; an empty collection of operation symbols leaves the hole/input and composite cases. At no point is an arrow lifted from a component evaluation, and the only equality detection in step 3 was proved from the given unit itself. Thus the final qualifications of the statement require no extra hypotheses.
